newsitem.title: ANGOLA: ANGOLA PREPARES TROOP WITHDRAWAL FROM DIAMOND AREA.
newsitem.headline: ANGOLA PREPARES TROOP WITHDRAWAL FROM DIAMOND AREA.

text.p: Angolan government troops were preparing to withdraw from positions in two of the country's most important diamond areas, an United Nations official said.
The U.N.'s military chief in Angola, General Phillip Sibanda, said the Angolan Armed Forces (FAA) had handed it a plan outlining the withdrawal from the Lundas provinces.
"We are studying the papers and should commence with the withdrawal before the end of the month," Sibanda told Reuters.
A FAA official confirmed the withdrawal of the troops to their nearest barracks, saying it was unconditional and was required by the government in terms with the Lusaka Protocol.
The Lusaka peace pact was signed in 1994 by the government and former rebel UNITA movement to end two decades of civil war which broke out at independence from Portugal in 1975.
Both the government and UNITA deployed soldiers in the Lunda provinces to guard their diamond interests.
It is estimated that UNITA earns between $300 million and $600 million per annum from diamonds.
Angola's government earns just over $200 million annually from diamonds and has sought talks with UNITA to equally carve up the area into concessions.
The government's diamond company, Endiama, began negotiations on the issue in June. Both sides have so far failed to agree on the future of the diamond area.
UNITA military chief General Arlindo Chenda Ben Ben told Reuters in an interview it was important that UNITA held onto its diamond areas to fund its political activities.

"Any political party has to survive with money and we are in some parts of the Lundas. We have our mining police and we have discussed this with the government and the Americans. We have to explore (diamonds) to have money," Ben Ben said.
